---
title: "Exploding Gradients"
description: "A training problem where gradient magnitudes grow excessively during backpropagation."
term: "Exploding Gradients"
letter: "E"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Exploding gradients occur when the gradients used to update model
parameters become extremely large. Training may become unstable, with
loss values or parameter updates growing rapidly.

## Technical explanation

In deep or recurrent computation graphs, repeated derivative
multiplications can amplify gradient magnitude. If the gradient norm
$\|g\|$ becomes large, an update such as
$\theta \leftarrow \theta-\eta g$ may produce an excessively large
parameter change.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Exploding gradients can prevent convergence, produce non-finite values,
and waste training compute. Diagnosing them helps teams choose suitable
initialization, optimization, architecture, and numerical-stability
strategies.

## How it works

During backpropagation, gradients flow through successive operations.
When their magnitudes are repeatedly amplified, the gradient reaching
earlier layers can become very large. Gradient clipping limits the norm
or values of gradients before the optimizer applies an update.

## Practical example

A training run may show a sudden jump in loss followed by `NaN`
parameters. Logging gradient norms and applying a justified clipping
threshold can help diagnose and mitigate the instability.

## Common misconceptions

- Gradient clipping can limit updates but does not explain or fix every
  underlying cause.
- Large gradients are not always evidence of an error; scale depends on
  the loss, data, and model.
- Exploding gradients and vanishing gradients are distinct problems,
  though both involve gradient propagation.
